author: Linda Cook
title: Judge rules on witness testimony in upcoming Trudy Appleby trial - NewsBreak
text:
By Linda Cook ,
4 hours ago
On Wednesday, a judge ruled on what witness testimony will be allowed in the upcoming trial of a man suspected in the death of an 11-year-old girl. Additionally, the trial may be moved from Henry County to a different county.
During Wednesday’s pretrial hearing, 51-year-old Jamison Fisher appeared in Henry County Court. Our Quad Cities News was in the courtroom, where Fisher sat calmly throughout the proceedings that lasted about two hours.
Judge Norma Kauzlarich read from a 104-page ruling that determines which witnesses can testify and the content of their testimony.
She ruled that Dennis Appleby, Trudy’s father, can take the stand under some restrictions: His testimony will be confined to his drug interactions with Fisher and David Whipple, the circumstances of those interactions, and the surrounding factual details; but not Appleby’s “own thoughts, feelings,or speculation” about Trudy’s disappearance.
Fisher is accused of killing Trudy Appleby. Her body has not been recovered.
Prosecutors filed murder charges against Fisher last year. The judge scheduled a hearing Sept. 4 to listen to arguments about whether to move the trial out of Henry County.
The court granted Fisher access to discovery material outside the courtroom, citing Fisher’s ADHD and the need for more time to review evidence. The judge gave Fisher a stern warning that any misuse of discovery material could result in revoking those privileges.
“I am telling you as of today once you get access to this discovery material, anything you do to violate my protective order will result in consequences,” Kauzlarich said.
The judge allowed witnesses who will testify that Fisher told them he killed Trudy.
The history of the case
Saturday, Aug. 1, will mark 30 years since Trudy’s disappearance in 1996. Last year, Henry County State’s Attorney Catherine Runty earlier said a grand jury indicted Fisher with three counts of first-degree murder and one count of concealment of a homicidal death. The statute of limitations prevented a charge of kidnapping because the case is so old, she said.
Investigators earlier said they believed David Whipple of Colona and Fisher knew about what happened to Trudy, and that they may be involved with the case. William “Ed” Smith, who was named a person of interest in 2017, is deceased. Whipple died in August 2022.
Trudy was last seen near her home in Moline. Over the years and during many vigils in her memory, her family pleaded for answers.
In August 2017, the Moline Police Department released information that a witness observed Trudy Appleby with William “Ed” Smith in a late model silver Chevrolet four-door near Smith’s residence on Campbell’s Island on Aug. 21, 1996, and listed Smith as a “person of interest” in the case.
David Whipple was the son-in-law of William “Ed” Smith and Jamison Fisher is a lifelong family friend of the Smiths, police said.
In 2020, Moline Police asked the community’s assistance regarding any information about William “Ed” Smith, David Whipple, and Fisher, and their involvement related to the disappearance of Trudy Appleby.
